1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: // Mechanical examiner of a code-safety report. It is in the report
3: // repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
4: //
5: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path>  one department's findings
6: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <path> --list-invalid
7: //   node verify-safety-report.mjs --report           the merged report
8: //
9: // `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
10: // `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
11: // stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
12: // learns which findings to drop and disclose.
13: //
14: // `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
15: // disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
16: // findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
17: //
18: // Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
19: // stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
20: // this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.
21: import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
22: import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
23: import { basename, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
24: 
25: /** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
26: const SEVERITIES = ['critical', 'high', 'medium', 'low', 'info']
27: 
28: /** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
29: const CONFIDENCES = ['confirmed', 'likely', 'possible']
30: 
31: /** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
32: const SECTIONS = [
33:   '## Résumé exécutif',
34:   '## Executive summary',
35:   '## Scope and method',
36:   '## Findings',
37:   '## What was not covered',
38:   '## Certificate',
39: ]
40: 
41: /** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */
42: const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
43: 
44: /** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
45: const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
46: 
47: /** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
48: const PLACEHOLDER = /\bTODO\b|\bTBD\b|\bFIXME\b|lorem ipsum|<placeholder>|PLACEHOLDER/i
49: 
50: /** String fields every finding states in prose. */
51: const PROSE_FIELDS = ['title', 'evidence', 'impact', 'fix']
52: 
53: /** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
54: const normalize = (text) => text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()
55: 
56: /** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
57: const sha256 = (content) => createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
58: 
59: /**
60:  * Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
61:  * @param {string} root directory to walk
62:  * @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
63:  * @returns {string[]} relative POSIX-ish paths, sorted
64:  */
65: function walk(root, exclude) {
66:   const found = []
67:   const descend = (directory) => {
68:     for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
69:       const path = join(directory, entry.name)
70:       if (entry.isDirectory()) {
71:         if (!exclude.includes(entry.name)) descend(path)
72:       } else if (entry.isFile()) found.push(relative(root, path))
73:     }
74:   }
75:   descend(root)
76:   return found.sort()
77: }
78: 
79: /** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
80: class Target {
81:   /**
82:    * @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
83:    * @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
84:    */
85:   constructor(reportRoot, failures) {
86:     this.failures = failures
87:     this.root = undefined
88:     this.files = new Map()
89:     this.lines = new Map()
90:     const lockPath = join(reportRoot, 'target.json')
91:     if (!existsSync(lockPath)) {
92:       failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
93:       return
94:     }
95:     const lock = JSON.parse(readFileSync(lockPath, 'utf8'))
96:     this.root = lock.root
97:     this.exclude = lock.exclude ?? []
98:     this.digest = lock.sha256
99:     for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
100:     this.checkTree()
101:   }
102: 
103:   /**
104:    * Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
105:    * cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
106:    * department edited is no longer that tree.
107:    */
108:   checkTree() {
109:     if (!existsSync(this.root)) {
110:       this.failures.push(`the target tree ${this.root} is not on this host, so no citation can be resolved`)
111:       this.root = undefined
112:       return
113:     }
114:     const present = walk(this.root, this.exclude)
115:     for (const path of present) {
116:       if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
117:     }
118:     for (const [path, hash] of this.files) {
119:       if (!present.includes(path)) {
120:         this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
121:         continue
122:       }
123:       if (sha256(readFileSync(join(this.root, path))) !== hash) {
124:         this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)
125:       }
126:     }
127:   }
128: 
129:   /**
130:    * The lines of one target file.
131:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
132:    * @returns {string[] | undefined} the file's lines, or undefined when it is not in the locked tree
133:    */
134:   linesOf(path) {
135:     if (this.root === undefined || !this.files.has(path)) return undefined
136:     if (!this.lines.has(path)) this.lines.set(path, readFileSync(join(this.root, path), 'utf8').split('\n'))
137:     return this.lines.get(path)
138:   }
139: 
140:   /**
141:    * Whether one `file:line` citation resolves in the locked tree.
142:    * @param {string} path path relative to the target root
143:    * @param {number} line 1-based line number
144:    * @returns {boolean} whether the file is under review and holds that line
145:    */
146:   resolves(path, line) {
147:     const lines = this.linesOf(path)
148:     return lines !== undefined && Number.isInteger(line) && line >= 1 && line <= lines.length
149:   }
150: }
151: 
152: /**
153:  * Decide one finding against the target tree.
154:  * @param {unknown} finding one entry of a findings file
155:  * @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id
156:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree the finding cites
157:  * @param {Set<string>} seen ids already used in this file
158:  * @returns {string[]} every rule this finding broke, empty when it holds
159:  */
160: function checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen) {
161:   const failures = []
162:   if (finding === null || typeof finding !== 'object' || Array.isArray(finding)) {
163:     return [`finding #${index + 1} is not a JSON object`]
164:   }
165:   const id = finding.id
166:   const name = typeof id === 'string' && id !== '' ? id : `#${index + 1}`
167:   const fail = (rule) => void failures.push(`${name}: ${rule}`)
168:   // Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
169:   // numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
170:   if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')
171:   else if (seen.has(id)) fail('id is used twice in this file')
172:   else seen.add(id)
173:   if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')
174:   if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')
175:   if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)
176:   if (!CONFIDENCES.includes(finding.confidence)) fail(`confidence must be one of ${CONFIDENCES.join(', ')}`)
177:   for (const field of PROSE_FIELDS) {
178:     if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
179:   }
180:   if (!Array.isArray(finding.references) || finding.references.some(reference => typeof reference !== 'string')) {
181:     fail('references must be an array of strings')
182:   }
183:   const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
184:   if (typeof file !== 'string' || file === '' || file.startsWith('/') || file.split('/').includes('..')) {
185:     fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
186:     return failures
187:   }
188:   const lines = target.linesOf(file)
189:   if (lines === undefined) {
190:     fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
191:     return failures
192:   }
193:   if (!Number.isInteger(line) || line < 1 || line > lines.length) {
194:     fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
195:     return failures
196:   }
197:   const last = endLine === undefined ? line : endLine
198:   if (!Number.isInteger(last) || last < line || last > lines.length) {
199:     fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
200:     return failures
201:   }
202:   if (typeof snippet !== 'string' || snippet.trim() === '') {
203:     fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
204:     return failures
205:   }
206:   const quoted = normalize(lines.slice(line - 1, last).join('\n'))
207:   if (normalize(snippet) !== quoted) {
208:     fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)
209:   }
210:   return failures
211: }
212: 
213: /**
214:  * Read one findings file.
215:  * @param {string} path the file to read
216:  * @param {string[]} failures collector a malformed file is reported on
217:  * @returns {unknown[]} the entries, empty when the file is missing or malformed
218:  */
219: function readFindings(path, failures) {
220:   if (!existsSync(path)) {
221:     failures.push(`${path} is missing`)
222:     return []
223:   }
224:   let parsed
225:   try {
226:     parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
227:   } catch (error) {
228:     failures.push(`${path} is not JSON: ${error.message}`)
229:     return []
230:   }
231:   if (!Array.isArray(parsed)) {
232:     failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
233:     return []
234:   }
235:   return parsed
236: }
237: 
238: /**
239:  * Decide one findings file on its own.
240:  * @param {string} path the findings file
241:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites
242:  * @returns {{ failures: string[], invalid: string[], findings: unknown[] }} the broken rules, the ids that broke them, and the entries
243:  */
244: function checkFindingsFile(path, target) {
245:   const failures = []
246:   const findings = readFindings(path, failures)
247:   const invalid = []
248:   const seen = new Set()
249:   findings.forEach((finding, index) => {
250:     const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
251:     if (broken.length === 0) return
252:     failures.push(...broken.map(rule => `${basename(path)}: ${rule}`))
253:     invalid.push(typeof finding?.id === 'string' ? finding.id : `#${index + 1}`)
254:   })
255:   return { failures, invalid, findings }
256: }
257: 
258: /**
259:  * The body of one section of the report.
260:  * @param {string} text the whole report
261:  * @param {string} heading the section heading, including its `##`
262:  * @returns {string} the text between this heading and the next one, empty when absent
263:  */
264: function section(text, heading) {
265:   const start = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
266:   if (start === -1) return ''
267:   const body = text.slice(start + heading.length + 1)
268:   const next = body.search(/^## /m)
269:   return next === -1 ? body : body.slice(0, next)
270: }
271: 
272: /**
273:  * Decide SAFETY-REPORT.md, findings.json and the disclosure of what was dropped.
274:  * @param {string} root the report repository
275:  * @param {Target} target the locked tree the report cites
276:  * @returns {string[]} every rule the report broke
277:  */
278: function checkReport(root, target) {
279:   const reportPath = join(root, 'SAFETY-REPORT.md')
280:   if (!existsSync(reportPath)) {
281:     return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
282:   }
283:   const text = readFileSync(reportPath, 'utf8')
284:   const failures = []
285:   let previous = -1
286:   for (const heading of SECTIONS) {
287:     const at = text.indexOf(`${heading}\n`)
288:     if (at === -1) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has no section ${JSON.stringify(heading)}`)
289:     else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
290:     else previous = at
291:   }
292:   const placeholder = PLACEHOLDER.exec(text)
293:   if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)
294:   const overclaim = OVERCLAIMS.exec(text)
295:   if (overclaim !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md claims more than this review supports: ${JSON.stringify(overclaim[0])}`)
296: 
297:   const union = checkFindingsFile(join(root, 'findings.json'), target)
298:   failures.push(...union.failures)
299:   const findings = union.findings.filter(finding => typeof finding?.id === 'string')
300: 
301:   const keys = new Set()
302:   for (const finding of findings) {
303:     const key = `${finding.file}:${finding.line}:${finding.cwe}`
304:     if (keys.has(key)) failures.push(`findings.json states ${key} twice; the union is deduplicated by file, line and cwe`)
305:     keys.add(key)
306:   }
307: 
308:   const listed = section(text, '## Findings')
309:   for (const finding of findings) {
310:     if (!listed.includes(finding.id)) failures.push(`the Findings section does not cite ${finding.id}`)
311:   }
312:   // The lookbehind keeps a URL's `host:port` out of the citation vocabulary:
313:   // the host is preceded by a slash, so no citation ever starts there.
314:   for (const [, path, line] of text.matchAll(/(?<![\w/.\-])([\w.-]+(?:\/[\w.-]+)*\.\w+):(\d+)\b/g)) {
315:     if (!target.resolves(path, Number(line))) failures.push(`the citation ${path}:${line} does not resolve in the tree under review`)
316:   }
317:

lines.text: // Mechanical examiner of a code-safety report. It is in the report
// repository's base commit, so no department can change what measures it.
// `--findings` decides one findings file against the target tree. Adding
// `--list-invalid` turns the same decision into a report: the failing ids go to
// stdout, one per line, and the exit code is 0, which is how the integration
// learns which findings to drop and disclose.
// `--report` decides SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json together, including the
// disclosure rule: every id any `findings/<department>.json` carries and
// findings.json does not must be named under `## What was not covered`.
// Exit 0 only when every rule holds; otherwise every failure is printed to
// stderr, one per line, and the exit code is 1. Node built-ins only, because
// this runs in a worktree that installs nothing.
import { basename, join, relative, resolve } from 'node:path'
/** Severities a finding may claim, most severe first. */
/** How sure a finding's author is that the cited code is exploitable as described. */
/** Sections SAFETY-REPORT.md carries, in this order. */
/** The claim the certificate must make verbatim, and the only claim this review supports. */

const HONESTY = 'This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".'
/** Claims no coverage this review can state would support. */
const OVERCLAIMS = /\bno vulnerabilities\b|\bfree of vulnerabilities\b|\b(?:is|are|was|were) secure\b|\bsafe to deploy\b|\bproven secure\b|\bfully audited\b/i
/** Text a report still carrying its template is refused for. */
/** String fields every finding states in prose. */
/** How a file's text is compared with a finding's quoted snippet. */
/** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of one buffer or string. */
* Every file under one directory, relative and sorted, skipping the excluded names.
* @param {string[]} exclude directory basenames never descended into
for (const entry of readdirSync(directory, { withFileTypes: true }).sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))) {
/** One target tree as the lock and the verifier both read it: the files, their digests, and their text. */
* @param {string} reportRoot the report repository the lock is committed in
* @param {string[]} failures collector every rule appends to
failures.push('target.json is missing from this worktree; the base commit carries the lock of the tree under review')
for (const [path, hash] of Object.entries(lock.files)) this.files.set(path, hash)
* Refuse a target that changed since the base commit locked it: a finding
* cites a line of the tree this program was asked to review, and a tree a
* department edited is no longer that tree.
this.failures.push(`the target tree ${this.root} is not on this host, so no citation can be resolved`)
if (!this.files.has(path)) this.failures.push(`the target tree gained ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
this.failures.push(`the target tree lost ${path} since the base commit locked it`)
this.failures.push(`the target tree's ${path} changed since the base commit locked it; the target is read-only for this program`)
* The lines of one target file.
* @param {string} path path relative to the target root
* @returns {string[] | undefined} the file's lines, or undefined when it is not in the locked tree
* Whether one `file:line` citation resolves in the locked tree.
* @param {string} path path relative to the target root
* @returns {boolean} whether the file is under review and holds that line
return lines !== undefined && Number.isInteger(line) && line >= 1 && line <= lines.length
* Decide one finding against the target tree.
* @param {unknown} finding one entry of a findings file
* @param {number} index its position, named when the entry has no usable id
* @param {Target} target the locked tree the finding cites
* @param {Set<string>} seen ids already used in this file
* @returns {string[]} every rule this finding broke, empty when it holds
return [`finding #${index + 1} is not a JSON object`]
const name = typeof id === 'string' && id !== '' ? id : `#${index + 1}`
// Letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`: wide enough for both the `SEC-001`
// numbering the knowledge pack's schema uses and a department-prefixed name.
if (typeof id !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.-]*$/.test(id)) fail('id must be letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores')
else if (seen.has(id)) fail('id is used twice in this file')
if (typeof finding.cwe !== 'string' || !/^CWE-\d+$/.test(finding.cwe)) fail('cwe must match CWE-<number>')
if (typeof finding.owasp !== 'string' || finding.owasp.trim() === '') fail('owasp must name the category')
if (!SEVERITIES.includes(finding.severity)) fail(`severity must be one of ${SEVERITIES.join(', ')}`)
if (!CONFIDENCES.includes(finding.confidence)) fail(`confidence must be one of ${CONFIDENCES.join(', ')}`)
if (typeof finding[field] !== 'string' || finding[field].trim() === '') fail(`${field} must be a non-empty string`)
fail('references must be an array of strings')
const { file, line, endLine, snippet } = finding
fail('file must be a path relative to the target root')
fail(`file ${file} is not in the tree under review`)
fail(`line ${JSON.stringify(line)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
const last = endLine === undefined ? line : endLine
fail(`endLine ${JSON.stringify(endLine)} is outside ${file}, which has ${lines.length} lines`)
fail('snippet must quote the cited line')
fail(`snippet does not match ${file}:${line}, which reads ${JSON.stringify(quoted.slice(0, 160))}`)
* @param {string[]} failures collector a malformed file is reported on
* @returns {unknown[]} the entries, empty when the file is missing or malformed
failures.push(`${path} must be a JSON array of findings`)
* Decide one findings file on its own.
* @param {Target} target the locked tree it cites
* @returns {{ failures: string[], invalid: string[], findings: unknown[] }} the broken rules, the ids that broke them, and the entries
const broken = checkFinding(finding, index, target, seen)
* The body of one section of the report.
* @param {string} heading the section heading, including its `##`
* @returns {string} the text between this heading and the next one, empty when absent
* Decide SAFETY-REPORT.md, findings.json and the disclosure of what was dropped.
* @param {Target} target the locked tree the report cites
return [`SAFETY-REPORT.md is missing; REPORTING.md in this worktree states the sections it carries: ${SECTIONS.join(', ')}`]
else if (at < previous) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md has ${JSON.stringify(heading)} out of order; the order is ${SECTIONS.join(' then ')}`)
if (placeholder !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md still carries placeholder text: ${JSON.stringify(placeholder[0])}`)
if (overclaim !== null) failures.push(`SAFETY-REPORT.md claims more than this review supports: ${JSON.stringify(overclaim[0])}`)
if (keys.has(key)) failures.push(`findings.json states ${key} twice; the union is deduplicated by file, line and cwe`)
if (!listed.includes(finding.id)) failures.push(`the Findings section does not cite ${finding.id}`)
// The lookbehind keeps a URL's `host:port` out of the citation vocabulary:
// the host is preceded by a slash, so no citation ever starts there.
if (!target.resolves(path, Number(line))) failures.push(`the citation ${path}:${line} does not resolve in the tree under review`)
for (const heading of ['## Résumé exécutif', '## Executive summary']) {
if (stated === null) failures.push(`${heading} does not state a "- ${severity}: <count>" line`)
const uncovered = section(text, '## What was not covered')
for (const finding of readFindings(join(department, entry), failures)) {
failures.push(`${id} was dropped from findings.json and is not disclosed under "## What was not covered"`)
if (!certificate.includes(HONESTY)) failures.push(`the Certificate must state, verbatim: ${JSON.stringify(HONESTY)}`)
if (stated === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Verified findings: <count>" line')
else if (Number(stated[1]) !== findings.length) failures.push(`the Certificate states ${stated[1]} verified findings, and findings.json holds ${findings.length}`)
if (tree === null) failures.push('the Certificate does not state a "Target tree: <sha256>" line')
else if (tree[1] !== target.digest) failures.push(`the Certificate states target tree ${tree[1]}, and target.json locks ${target.digest}`)
// A department that found nothing states `[]` and says so in its report
// section: requiring a finding would buy one by inventing it.
if (failures.length === 0) console.log(`ok: SAFETY-REPORT.md and findings.json verified against ${target.root}`)

  {
    "id": "access-adminshowusers-cookie-privilege",

## Executive summary

This integrated review covers dvja (Damn Vulnerable Java Application), a Java Struts2/Spring/Hibernate app, over the tree locked at `/home/user/targets/dvja` (174 files, sha256 `014b5713f91d7c23181b282f75b1e8220f54f5d5de5e0ea36f28e1c456a80982`). Six departments (access, data, dependencies, injection, platform, secrets) each read the code and produced their own findings; this integration merges their 43 findings into 40, after removing 3 exact duplicates (same file, line and CWE) and with no finding invalidated by the mechanical examiner. Breakdown: 9 critical, 10 high, 13 medium, 7 low, 1 info. The three most important: (1) a password-reset key that is nothing more than MD5 of the login, with no secret or expiry, giving unauthenticated account takeover (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:90`); (2) full export of every user's data via `/api/userList`, authorized purely by a caller-forged `admin=1` cookie on a route that also passes through no authentication interceptor at all (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:39-44` and `src/main/resources/struts.xml:156-159`); (3) three confirmed SQL/JPQL injections and one OS command injection, each traced end-to-end from request parameter to sink (`UserService.java:75`, `ProductService.java:48`, `PingAction.java:45`). Coverage included the Struts entry points, the Java controllers and services, the data model, the JSP views cited by a finding, the Struts/Spring/Log4j2/Docker configuration, and `pom.xml`; it did not cover actual runtime behavior, git history, vendored third-party front-end libraries (jQuery, Font Awesome), full transitive-dependency resolution, or any dynamic testing (see "What was not covered"). Method: entry points first, data traced from source to sink, one finding per sink, exact line quoted, confidence stated, then every finding mechanically verified against the locked tree by `verify-safety-report.mjs`.

## Scope and method

Target: `/home/user/targets/dvja`, locked in `target.json` to 174 files (only `.git` excluded) under sha256 `014b5713f91d7c23181b282f75b1e8220f54f5d5de5e0ea36f28e1c456a80982`. Six departments ran on their own branches and each committed `findings/<department>.json` and `report/<department>.md`: **access** (authentication, session handling, authorization, CSRF), **data** (sensitive-data exposure, crypto misuse, logging), **dependencies** (`pom.xml` manifest review against the OSV advisory database), **injection** (SQL/JPQL, OS command, XSS, open redirect), **platform** (security headers, cookies, error handling, devMode, container configuration) and **secrets** (hard-coded credentials). This integration is itself a language-model review: it read every department's `findings/*.json` and `report/*.md` in full and is grounded by two mechanical checks — `verify-safety-report.mjs` (the committed examiner, which re-hashes the locked tree and checks every citation and snippet), and, for the dependencies department only, live queries against the OSV API (`api.osv.dev`, ecosystem Maven) for each directly declared `pom.xml` coordinate. **No static-analysis scanner (e.g. semgrep) was run by any department in this engagement** — every report says so explicitly, and this integration repeats it rather than implying a scanner ran: all findings below come from a department reading source code directly, not from pattern-matched tool output.

Files the six departments state they actually opened and traced (not merely the full 174-file list that exists in the tree): `src/main/resources/struts.xml` and `example.xml`; every controller under `src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/`; every service under `src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/`; `AuthenticationInterceptor.java`, `Constant.java`, `models/User.java`, `models/Product.java`; `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml`, `config.properties`, `applicationContext.xml`; `src/main/resources/log4j2.xml`, `persistence.xml`; `pom.xml`; `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/start.sh`; a sample of the JSP views directly implicated by a finding (`UserEdit.jsp`, `UserSearch.jsp`, `ProductList.jsp`, `ProductEdit.jsp`, `Ping.jsp`, `Home.jsp`, `index.html`); and the `com.appsecco.example` tutorial package (read, found to hold no sink). Method follows the review-method skill throughout: entry points first, each attacker- or user-controlled field traced from its Struts action binding to its sink (a query, a shell command, a log statement, an HTML render, a redirect, or a stored/declared credential), one finding per sink, the exact cited line quoted and re-checked against the target's own text by the examiner, and a stated confidence (`confirmed`, `likely`, or `possible`) per finding. This is a static, read-only review: the target tree was never modified, and no department stood up a running instance of the application.

## Findings

### critical

- `access-reset-password-predictable-token` — Password-reset token is a deterministic MD5 of the public login name, not a server-issued secret (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:90`, CWE-640, confirmed) — anyone who knows or guesses a login can compute a valid reset key themselves and take over that account, including an administrator's; fix by generating a random, stored, single-use, expiring token instead.
- `data-006` — Bulk export of every user's PII is gated only by a client-supplied cookie (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:40`, CWE-602, confirmed) — any caller who sends `Cookie: admin=1` receives the full user directory; fix by deleting the cookie check and requiring a server-side session role check behind an authentication interceptor.
- `dependencies-struts2-core` — Apache Struts2 2.3.30 carries multiple pre-authentication RCE advisories, including the Equifax-breach CVE-2017-5638 (`pom.xml:22`, CWE-20, confirmed) — an unauthenticated attacker can execute arbitrary code with a single crafted HTTP request; fix by upgrading to a currently supported Struts 6.x (or at minimum 2.5.33) release.
- `dependencies-log4j-core` — log4j-core 2.3 is vulnerable to Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) and is wired in as the framework's active logger (`pom.xml:47`, CWE-502, likely) — if any Log4j2-backed log statement ever carries attacker text, unauthenticated remote code execution follows; fix by upgrading to 2.17.1 or later and removing the conflicting `slf4j-log4j12` binding.
- `injection-sqli-user-search` — SQL injection in user login search via string-concatenated JPQL (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:75`, CWE-89, confirmed) — any authenticated user can inject JPQL to dump arbitrary rows; fix by using the parameterized query the file already has two methods above.
- `injection-sqli-product-search` — SQL injection in product listing search via a string-concatenated JPQL LIKE clause (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/ProductService.java:48`, CWE-89, confirmed) — enumerates or exfiltrates arbitrary rows; fix by binding the value as a parameter.
- `injection-cmdi-ping` — OS command injection in the ping diagnostic feature (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/PingAction.java:45`, CWE-78, confirmed) — any authenticated user can run arbitrary shell commands as the application's OS user; fix by validating the address as a strict IP/hostname and executing without a shell.
- `platform-001` — Struts2 developer mode (devMode) is enabled, exposing debug diagnostics and potentially the OGNL debugging console (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:7`, CWE-489, likely) — unauthenticated requests that trigger an error can leak internals or worse; fix by setting `struts.devMode` to `false` for any non-developer deployment.
- `platform-006` — Admin user-list API trusts a client-supplied cookie instead of a server-side authorization check (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:39`, CWE-602, confirmed) — any unauthenticated client sending `Cookie: admin=1` receives the full user directory; fix by authorizing from server-side session/role state instead.

### high

- `access-api-userlist-noauth` — `/api/userList.action` has no authentication interceptor at all (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:158`, CWE-862, confirmed) — the admin user-list handler is reachable with zero session state; fix by adding the authentication interceptor stack to the `api` package.
- `access-adminshowusers-cookie-privilege` — Admin capability is self-assigned via a client-supplied cookie, not the user's stored role (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:40`, CWE-863, confirmed) — any caller can grant themselves the admin branch of the handler; fix by gating on the session user's stored role.
- `access-edituser-missing-csrf` — `editUser` (password/email change) has no CSRF token, enabling forced password change (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:62`, CWE-352, confirmed) — a single clicked link changes a victim's password to a value the attacker knows; fix by adding a token interceptor and a CSRF hidden field.
- `data-001` — Passwords hashed with unsalted MD5 instead of a slow, salted hash (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:109`, CWE-327, confirmed) — a leaked `users` table is trivially crackable; fix by moving to BCrypt/Argon2id.
- `data-005` — Unauthenticated API endpoint discloses any user's email address (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:79`, CWE-200, confirmed) — enables account enumeration and phishing with no login required; fix by requiring authentication and not returning another user's email.
- `injection-xss-stored-product-name` — Stored XSS in product name rendered with escaping disabled (`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/dvja/ProductList.jsp:42`, CWE-79, confirmed) — a malicious product name executes in every viewer's browser; fix by removing `escape="false"`.
- `platform-007` — The `/api` Struts package has no authentication interceptor, so every action in it runs unauthenticated (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:156`, CWE-306, confirmed) — any future action added to this package inherits no login requirement; fix by adding the authentication interceptor to the package.
- `dvja-secrets-001` — MySQL root password hard-coded in committed `docker-compose.yml` (mysql service) (`docker-compose.yml:8`, CWE-798, confirmed) — anyone with repository access has the database container's root credential; fix by moving it to an untracked `.env`/secret and rotating it.
- `dvja-secrets-002` — Same MySQL root password re-declared for the app service and used by `start.sh` to run schema DDL as root (`docker-compose.yml:17`, CWE-798, confirmed) — the running app container's own DB credential is committed in plaintext; fix by using a low-privilege account and externalizing the value.
- `dvja-secrets-003` — MySQL root password hard-coded in the deployed application's `config.properties` and wired into the live Spring DataSource (`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/config.properties:4`, CWE-798, confirmed) — the credential the running application actually uses for every query is recoverable from the WAR/source; fix by externalizing via environment/secrets manager and using least privilege.

### medium

- `access-addeditproduct-missing-csrf` — `addEditProduct` (create/update product) has no CSRF token (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:79`, CWE-352, confirmed) — a cross-site form can create/overwrite products as any logged-in user; fix by adding a token interceptor and CSRF field.
- `access-login-no-session-regeneration` — Session id is not regenerated after successful login (session fixation) (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/Login.java:50`, CWE-384, likely) — a pre-login fixed session id becomes fully authenticated once the victim logs in; fix by invalidating and reissuing the session id on login.
- `access-logout-session-not-invalidated` — Logout removes the user attribute but never invalidates the underlying session (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/Login.java:39`, CWE-613, confirmed) — the container session and its id survive logout; fix by calling `HttpSession.invalidate()` on logout.
- `access-login-no-rate-limit` — Login has no attempt limit, lockout or delay (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/Login.java:49`, CWE-307, confirmed) — online brute-forcing is practical against any known login; fix by adding a per-account attempt counter with backoff/lockout.
- `data-002` — New password logged in cleartext during password reset (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:93`, CWE-532, confirmed) — anyone with log access obtains a user's plaintext new password; fix by removing the password value from the log statement.
- `data-004` — Struts2 devMode is enabled, exposing debug information to clients (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:7`, CWE-215, likely) — verbose stack traces reach error responses; fix by disabling devMode for deployment.
- `dependencies-mysql-connector` — mysql-connector-java 5.1.42 is affected by multiple Connector/J privilege-management advisories (`pom.xml:135`, CWE-269, likely) — exploitable primarily by a malicious/compromised database server; fix by upgrading to at least 8.2.0.
- `injection-xss-reflected-product-search` — Reflected XSS in product search results via raw scriptlet output (`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/dvja/ProductList.jsp:23`, CWE-79, confirmed) — a crafted search link runs attacker JavaScript in a victim's session; fix by using the auto-escaping `<s:property>` tag.
- `injection-open-redirect` — Unvalidated open redirect via the `url` request parameter (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:101`, CWE-601, confirmed) — a trusted-domain link can send victims to an attacker site; fix by validating `url` against an allowlist.
- `platform-002` — Struts2 config-browser debug plugin is shipped in the production build (`pom.xml:26`, CWE-489, likely) — an unauthenticated visitor can enumerate the app's action/interceptor configuration; fix by removing the plugin or scoping it to test.
- `platform-003` — No security-headers filter is mounted: CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and HSTS are all absent (`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml:13`, CWE-1021, confirmed) — responses can be framed, MIME-sniffed, or served without HSTS; fix by adding a security-headers filter ahead of the Struts2 filter.

- `platform-005` — Raw exception message from a database query is returned to the client on the user-search form (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/UserAction.java:115`, CWE-209, confirmed) — discloses the internal query shape and confirms the injection point; fix by returning a generic message and logging the detail server-side.

- `access-password-compare-non-constant-time` — Password hash comparison uses `String.equals()`, not a constant-time comparison (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:52`, CWE-208, confirmed) — a secondary weakness on top of unsalted MD5 storage; fix by using `MessageDigest.isEqual()` and a salted adaptive hash.
- `access-api-ping-unauth-identifier-trust` — `/api/ping.action` trusts a caller-supplied login and discloses the account's email with no authentication (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:157`, CWE-862, confirmed) — enables login/email enumeration; fix by requiring authentication and scoping to the caller's own account.
- `dependencies-slf4j-log4j12` — slf4j-log4j12 1.5.2 is a 2008-era, unmaintained binding that transitively pulls end-of-life Log4j 1.x (`pom.xml:53`, CWE-1104, possible) — no upstream fix path for that classpath component; fix by removing it and routing logging through Log4j 2.
- `dependencies-gson` — gson 2.8.1 matches CVE-2022-25647, but the app's own code only calls the serializing `toJson`, not the vulnerable `fromJson` sink (`pom.xml:141`, CWE-502, possible) — not currently reachable through this app's own code; fix by upgrading to 2.8.9+ regardless.
- `dependencies-hibernate-3x` — hibernate-core/entitymanager/annotations pin a 2009-2010 Hibernate 3.x line with no upstream support (`pom.xml:99`, CWE-1104, possible) — any future ORM issue has no vendor fix path; fix by migrating to a maintained 5.6.x/6.x line.
- `platform-008` — Open redirect: the redirect action forwards to an attacker-supplied URL with no validation (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:100`, CWE-601, confirmed) — aids phishing from a trusted domain; fix by validating `url` against an allowlist.

- `dependencies-spring-3x` — spring-tx and spring-orm are pinned to Spring Framework 3.0.5.RELEASE (2011), a line with no upstream support (`pom.xml:122`, CWE-1104, possible) — no specific CVE was found for this exact coordinate, reported as a maintenance concern only; fix by upgrading to a supported Spring 5.x/6.x release.

- **Dropped as an exact duplicate**: `platform-009` (`docker-compose.yml:8`, CWE-798) reported the identical file, line and CWE as `dvja-secrets-001`; both were `confidence: confirmed` and both passed the examiner individually. The union keeps the `secrets` department's entry and drops `platform-009`.
- No finding from any department's `findings/*.json` was invalidated by the mechanical examiner (`node verify-safety-report.mjs --findings <file> --list-invalid` printed nothing for any of the six files); the three drops above are dedup-only, not correctness rulings.
- **No static-analysis scanner ran**: every one of the six department reports states plainly that `semgrep` (or any other pattern-matching scanner) was not invoked in that department's pass. Every finding in this program, and therefore in this report, comes from a language model reading source code directly and citing exact lines, checked afterward by the mechanical examiner — not from scanner output.
- **No dynamic testing**: no department stood up a running instance of dvja or sent it a live HTTP request (no exploit was executed for the SQL injection, command injection, XSS, CSRF, or reset-token findings); every finding is a static source-to-sink trace.
- **Git history was not inspected** by any department (no `git log -p`, no secret-scanning of historical blobs): only the working tree at the commit `target.json` locks was read, so an earlier, different value for the committed MySQL password (or a secret since removed) would not be found here.

- **Compiled third-party jars were not opened**: Struts2/XWork internals, the Log4j2 internals, and the Hibernate 3.x internals are not among the 174 tracked source files and were not decompiled; this is why the devMode console (`platform-001`), the config-browser plugin's exact route (`platform-002`), the Log4j2-vs-Log4j-1.x call-site question (`dependencies-log4j-core`), and Jetty's actual default cookie flags (`platform-004`) are all `likely`/`possible` rather than `confirmed`.
- **Vendored front-end assets were not audited for their own CVEs**: `src/main/webapp/assets/jquery-3.2.1.min.js`, `showdown.min.js`, and the Font Awesome `assets/fa/**` tree were grepped for obvious DOM-sink patterns (`postMessage`, `innerHTML`, `document.write`, `eval`) with no application-authored hits, but the project has no manifest (`package.json`) declaring these versions, so they were not turned into dependency findings and their own known advisories (if any) were not queried.
- **Documentation and IDE metadata were not treated as reviewable code**: `docs/**` (the project's own OWASP-training walkthroughs), `README.md`, and `.idea/**` project files were opened only far enough to confirm they hold no embedded credential or executable logic; they were not otherwise assessed for content (e.g. a documented example reset-key URL in `docs/solution/a2-broken-authentication-and-session-management.md` is training prose, not a value the running service reads, and is not cited as a finding here).

- **Runtime/network transport** (whether TLS terminates in front of this app via a reverse proxy) is infrastructure outside the locked source tree and cannot be confirmed by a static read either way; no finding above claims a transport-security conclusion.

## Certificate

Verified findings: 40
Target tree: 014b5713f91d7c23181b282f75b1e8220f54f5d5de5e0ea36f28e1c456a80982

`node verify-safety-report.mjs --report` mechanically confirmed that all 40 findings in `findings.json` resolve to a real file and line in the locked tree above, with each quoted snippet matching the target's own text at that line (whitespace-insensitive); that all 40 ids are unique; that no two findings share file, line and CWE; that every id any department's `findings/*.json` carries and this file does not is disclosed above under "What was not covered"; and that the severity counts stated in the summaries match the union exactly.

This review does not certify the absence of vulnerabilities; it certifies only that each listed finding was mechanically verified to exist at the cited line, over the files listed in "Scope and method".

## Executive summary

This integrated review covers dvja (Damn Vulnerable Java Application), a Java Struts2/Spring/Hibernate app, over the tree locked at `/home/user/targets/dvja` (174 files, sha256 `014b5713f91d7c23181b282f75b1e8220f54f5d5de5e0ea36f28e1c456a80982`). Six departments (access, data, dependencies, injection, platform, secrets) each read the code and produced their own findings; this integration merges their 43 findings into 40, after removing 3 exact duplicates (same file, line and CWE) and with no finding invalidated by the mechanical examiner. Breakdown: 9 critical, 10 high, 13 medium, 7 low, 1 info. The three most important: (1) a password-reset key that is nothing more than MD5 of the login, with no secret or expiry, giving unauthenticated account takeover (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:90`); (2) full export of every user's data via `/api/userList`, authorized purely by a caller-forged `admin=1` cookie on a route that also passes through no authentication interceptor at all (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:39-44` and `src/main/resources/struts.xml:156-159`); (3) three confirmed SQL/JPQL injections and one OS command injection, each traced end-to-end from request parameter to sink (`UserService.java:75`, `ProductService.java:48`, `PingAction.java:45`). Coverage included the Struts entry points, the Java controllers and services, the data model, the JSP views cited by a finding, the Struts/Spring/Log4j2/Docker configuration, and `pom.xml`; it did not cover actual runtime behavior, git history, vendored third-party front-end libraries (jQuery, Font Awesome), full transitive-dependency resolution, or any dynamic testing (see "What was not covered"). Method: entry points first, data traced from source to sink, one finding per sink, exact line quoted, confidence stated, then every finding mechanically verified against the locked tree by `verify-safety-report.mjs`.

## Scope and method

Target: `/home/user/targets/dvja`, locked in `target.json` to 174 files (only `.git` excluded) under sha256 `014b5713f91d7c23181b282f75b1e8220f54f5d5de5e0ea36f28e1c456a80982`. Six departments ran on their own branches and each committed `findings/<department>.json` and `report/<department>.md`: **access** (authentication, session handling, authorization, CSRF), **data** (sensitive-data exposure, crypto misuse, logging), **dependencies** (`pom.xml` manifest review against the OSV advisory database), **injection** (SQL/JPQL, OS command, XSS, open redirect), **platform** (security headers, cookies, error handling, devMode, container configuration) and **secrets** (hard-coded credentials). This integration is itself a language-model review: it read every department's `findings/*.json` and `report/*.md` in full and is grounded by two mechanical checks — `verify-safety-report.mjs` (the committed examiner, which re-hashes the locked tree and checks every citation and snippet), and, for the dependencies department only, live queries against the OSV API (`api.osv.dev`, ecosystem Maven) for each directly declared `pom.xml` coordinate. **No static-analysis scanner (e.g. semgrep) was run by any department in this engagement** — every report says so explicitly, and this integration repeats it rather than implying a scanner ran: all findings below come from a department reading source code directly, not from pattern-matched tool output.

Files the six departments state they actually opened and traced (not merely the full 174-file list that exists in the tree): `src/main/resources/struts.xml` and `example.xml`; every controller under `src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/`; every service under `src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/`; `AuthenticationInterceptor.java`, `Constant.java`, `models/User.java`, `models/Product.java`; `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml`, `config.properties`, `applicationContext.xml`; `src/main/resources/log4j2.xml`, `persistence.xml`; `pom.xml`; `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/start.sh`; a sample of the JSP views directly implicated by a finding (`UserEdit.jsp`, `UserSearch.jsp`, `ProductList.jsp`, `ProductEdit.jsp`, `Ping.jsp`, `Home.jsp`, `index.html`); and the `com.appsecco.example` tutorial package (read, found to hold no sink). Method follows the review-method skill throughout: entry points first, each attacker- or user-controlled field traced from its Struts action binding to its sink (a query, a shell command, a log statement, an HTML render, a redirect, or a stored/declared credential), one finding per sink, the exact cited line quoted and re-checked against the target's own text by the examiner, and a stated confidence (`confirmed`, `likely`, or `possible`) per finding. This is a static, read-only review: the target tree was never modified, and no department stood up a running instance of the application.

## Findings

### critical

- `access-reset-password-predictable-token` — Password-reset token is a deterministic MD5 of the public login name, not a server-issued secret (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:90`, CWE-640, confirmed) — anyone who knows or guesses a login can compute a valid reset key themselves and take over that account, including an administrator's; fix by generating a random, stored, single-use, expiring token instead.
- `data-006` — Bulk export of every user's PII is gated only by a client-supplied cookie (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:40`, CWE-602, confirmed) — any caller who sends `Cookie: admin=1` receives the full user directory; fix by deleting the cookie check and requiring a server-side session role check behind an authentication interceptor.
- `dependencies-struts2-core` — Apache Struts2 2.3.30 carries multiple pre-authentication RCE advisories, including the Equifax-breach CVE-2017-5638 (`pom.xml:22`, CWE-20, confirmed) — an unauthenticated attacker can execute arbitrary code with a single crafted HTTP request; fix by upgrading to a currently supported Struts 6.x (or at minimum 2.5.33) release.
- `dependencies-log4j-core` — log4j-core 2.3 is vulnerable to Log4Shell (CVE-2021-44228) and is wired in as the framework's active logger (`pom.xml:47`, CWE-502, likely) — if any Log4j2-backed log statement ever carries attacker text, unauthenticated remote code execution follows; fix by upgrading to 2.17.1 or later and removing the conflicting `slf4j-log4j12` binding.
- `injection-sqli-user-search` — SQL injection in user login search via string-concatenated JPQL (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:75`, CWE-89, confirmed) — any authenticated user can inject JPQL to dump arbitrary rows; fix by using the parameterized query the file already has two methods above.
- `injection-sqli-product-search` — SQL injection in product listing search via a string-concatenated JPQL LIKE clause (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/ProductService.java:48`, CWE-89, confirmed) — enumerates or exfiltrates arbitrary rows; fix by binding the value as a parameter.
- `injection-cmdi-ping` — OS command injection in the ping diagnostic feature (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/PingAction.java:45`, CWE-78, confirmed) — any authenticated user can run arbitrary shell commands as the application's OS user; fix by validating the address as a strict IP/hostname and executing without a shell.
- `platform-001` — Struts2 developer mode (devMode) is enabled, exposing debug diagnostics and potentially the OGNL debugging console (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:7`, CWE-489, likely) — unauthenticated requests that trigger an error can leak internals or worse; fix by setting `struts.devMode` to `false` for any non-developer deployment.
- `platform-006` — Admin user-list API trusts a client-supplied cookie instead of a server-side authorization check (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:39`, CWE-602, confirmed) — any unauthenticated client sending `Cookie: admin=1` receives the full user directory; fix by authorizing from server-side session/role state instead.

### high

- `access-api-userlist-noauth` — `/api/userList.action` has no authentication interceptor at all (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:158`, CWE-862, confirmed) — the admin user-list handler is reachable with zero session state; fix by adding the authentication interceptor stack to the `api` package.
- `access-adminshowusers-cookie-privilege` — Admin capability is self-assigned via a client-supplied cookie, not the user's stored role (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:40`, CWE-863, confirmed) — any caller can grant themselves the admin branch of the handler; fix by gating on the session user's stored role.
- `access-edituser-missing-csrf` — `editUser` (password/email change) has no CSRF token, enabling forced password change (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:62`, CWE-352, confirmed) — a single clicked link changes a victim's password to a value the attacker knows; fix by adding a token interceptor and a CSRF hidden field.
- `data-001` — Passwords hashed with unsalted MD5 instead of a slow, salted hash (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:109`, CWE-327, confirmed) — a leaked `users` table is trivially crackable; fix by moving to BCrypt/Argon2id.
- `data-005` — Unauthenticated API endpoint discloses any user's email address (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:79`, CWE-200, confirmed) — enables account enumeration and phishing with no login required; fix by requiring authentication and not returning another user's email.
- `injection-xss-stored-product-name` — Stored XSS in product name rendered with escaping disabled (`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/dvja/ProductList.jsp:42`, CWE-79, confirmed) — a malicious product name executes in every viewer's browser; fix by removing `escape="false"`.
- `platform-007` — The `/api` Struts package has no authentication interceptor, so every action in it runs unauthenticated (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:156`, CWE-306, confirmed) — any future action added to this package inherits no login requirement; fix by adding the authentication interceptor to the package.
- `dvja-secrets-001` — MySQL root password hard-coded in committed `docker-compose.yml` (mysql service) (`docker-compose.yml:8`, CWE-798, confirmed) — anyone with repository access has the database container's root credential; fix by moving it to an untracked `.env`/secret and rotating it.
- `dvja-secrets-002` — Same MySQL root password re-declared for the app service and used by `start.sh` to run schema DDL as root (`docker-compose.yml:17`, CWE-798, confirmed) — the running app container's own DB credential is committed in plaintext; fix by using a low-privilege account and externalizing the value.
- `dvja-secrets-003` — MySQL root password hard-coded in the deployed application's `config.properties` and wired into the live Spring DataSource (`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/config.properties:4`, CWE-798, confirmed) — the credential the running application actually uses for every query is recoverable from the WAR/source; fix by externalizing via environment/secrets manager and using least privilege.

### medium

- `access-addeditproduct-missing-csrf` — `addEditProduct` (create/update product) has no CSRF token (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:79`, CWE-352, confirmed) — a cross-site form can create/overwrite products as any logged-in user; fix by adding a token interceptor and CSRF field.
- `access-login-no-session-regeneration` — Session id is not regenerated after successful login (session fixation) (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/Login.java:50`, CWE-384, likely) — a pre-login fixed session id becomes fully authenticated once the victim logs in; fix by invalidating and reissuing the session id on login.
- `access-logout-session-not-invalidated` — Logout removes the user attribute but never invalidates the underlying session (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/Login.java:39`, CWE-613, confirmed) — the container session and its id survive logout; fix by calling `HttpSession.invalidate()` on logout.
- `access-login-no-rate-limit` — Login has no attempt limit, lockout or delay (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/Login.java:49`, CWE-307, confirmed) — online brute-forcing is practical against any known login; fix by adding a per-account attempt counter with backoff/lockout.
- `data-002` — New password logged in cleartext during password reset (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:93`, CWE-532, confirmed) — anyone with log access obtains a user's plaintext new password; fix by removing the password value from the log statement.
- `data-004` — Struts2 devMode is enabled, exposing debug information to clients (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:7`, CWE-215, likely) — verbose stack traces reach error responses; fix by disabling devMode for deployment.
- `dependencies-mysql-connector` — mysql-connector-java 5.1.42 is affected by multiple Connector/J privilege-management advisories (`pom.xml:135`, CWE-269, likely) — exploitable primarily by a malicious/compromised database server; fix by upgrading to at least 8.2.0.
- `injection-xss-reflected-product-search` — Reflected XSS in product search results via raw scriptlet output (`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/dvja/ProductList.jsp:23`, CWE-79, confirmed) — a crafted search link runs attacker JavaScript in a victim's session; fix by using the auto-escaping `<s:property>` tag.
- `injection-open-redirect` — Unvalidated open redirect via the `url` request parameter (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:101`, CWE-601, confirmed) — a trusted-domain link can send victims to an attacker site; fix by validating `url` against an allowlist.
- `platform-002` — Struts2 config-browser debug plugin is shipped in the production build (`pom.xml:26`, CWE-489, likely) — an unauthenticated visitor can enumerate the app's action/interceptor configuration; fix by removing the plugin or scoping it to test.
- `platform-003` — No security-headers filter is mounted: CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and HSTS are all absent (`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml:13`, CWE-1021, confirmed) — responses can be framed, MIME-sniffed, or served without HSTS; fix by adding a security-headers filter ahead of the Struts2 filter.
- `platform-004` — Session cookie has no explicit Secure, HttpOnly or SameSite configuration (`src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml:32`, CWE-614, likely) — the session cookie can be sent over plain HTTP and is more exposed to cross-site delivery; fix by adding an explicit `<session-config><cookie-config>` block.
- `platform-005` — Raw exception message from a database query is returned to the client on the user-search form (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/UserAction.java:115`, CWE-209, confirmed) — discloses the internal query shape and confirms the injection point; fix by returning a generic message and logging the detail server-side.

### low

- `access-password-compare-non-constant-time` — Password hash comparison uses `String.equals()`, not a constant-time comparison (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:52`, CWE-208, confirmed) — a secondary weakness on top of unsalted MD5 storage; fix by using `MessageDigest.isEqual()` and a salted adaptive hash.
- `access-api-ping-unauth-identifier-trust` — `/api/ping.action` trusts a caller-supplied login and discloses the account's email with no authentication (`src/main/resources/struts.xml:157`, CWE-862, confirmed) — enables login/email enumeration; fix by requiring authentication and scoping to the caller's own account.
- `dependencies-slf4j-log4j12` — slf4j-log4j12 1.5.2 is a 2008-era, unmaintained binding that transitively pulls end-of-life Log4j 1.x (`pom.xml:53`, CWE-1104, possible) — no upstream fix path for that classpath component; fix by removing it and routing logging through Log4j 2.

## Executive summary

Method: entry points first, data traced from source to sink, one finding per sink, exact line quoted, confidence stated, then every finding mechanically verified against the locked tree by `verify-safety-report.mjs`.

## Scope and method

Target: `/home/user/targets/dvja`, locked in `target.json` to 174 files (only `.git` excluded) under sha256 `014b5713f91d7c23181b282f75b1e8220f54f5d5de5e0ea36f28e1c456a80982`. Six departments ran on their own branches and each committed `findings/<department>.json` and `report/<department>.md`: **access** (authentication, session handling, authorization, CSRF), **data** (sensitive-data exposure, crypto misuse, logging), **dependencies** (`pom.xml` manifest review against the OSV advisory database), **injection** (SQL/JPQL, OS command, XSS, open redirect), **platform** (security headers, cookies, error handling, devMode, container configuration) and **secrets** (hard-coded credentials). This integration is itself a language-model review: it read every department's `findings/*.json` and `report/*.md` in full and is grounded by two mechanical checks — `verify-safety-report.mjs` (the committed examiner, which re-hashes the locked tree and checks every citation and snippet), and, for the dependencies department only, live queries against the OSV API (`api.osv.dev`, ecosystem Maven) for each directly declared `pom.xml` coordinate. **No static-analysis scanner (e.g. semgrep) was run by any department in this engagement** — every report says so explicitly, and this integration repeats it rather than implying a scanner ran: all findings below come from a department reading source code directly, not from pattern-matched tool output.

Files the six departments state they actually opened and traced (not merely the full 174-file list that exists in the tree): `src/main/resources/struts.xml` and `example.xml`; every controller under `src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/`; every service under `src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/`; `AuthenticationInterceptor.java`, `Constant.java`, `models/User.java`, `models/Product.java`; `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml`, `config.properties`, `applicationContext.xml`; `src/main/resources/log4j2.xml`, `persistence.xml`; `pom.xml`; `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/start.sh`; a sample of the JSP views directly implicated by a finding (`UserEdit.jsp`, `UserSearch.jsp`, `ProductList.jsp`, `ProductEdit.jsp`, `Ping.jsp`, `Home.jsp`, `index.html`); and the `com.appsecco.example` tutorial package (read, found to hold no sink). Method follows the review-method skill throughout: entry points first, each attacker- or user-controlled field traced from its Struts action binding to its sink (a query, a shell command, a log statement, an HTML render, a redirect, or a stored/declared credential), one finding per sink, the exact cited line quoted and re-checked against the target's own text by the examiner, and a stated confidence (`confirmed`, `likely`, or `possible`) per finding. ## Executive summary

This integrated review covers dvja (Damn Vulnerable Java Application), a Java Struts2/Spring/Hibernate app, over the tree locked at `/home/user/targets/dvja` (174 files, sha256 `014b5713f91d7c23181b282f75b1e8220f54f5d5de5e0ea36f28e1c456a80982`). Six departments (access, data, dependencies, injection, platform, secrets) each read the code and produced their own findings; this integration merges their 43 findings into 40, after removing 3 exact duplicates (same file, line and CWE) and with no finding invalidated by the mechanical examiner. Breakdown: 9 critical, 10 high, 13 medium, 7 low, 1 info. The three most important: (1) a password-reset key that is nothing more than MD5 of the login, with no secret or expiry, giving unauthenticated account takeover (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/services/UserService.java:90`); (2) full export of every user's data via `/api/userList`, authorized purely by a caller-forged `admin=1` cookie on a route that also passes through no authentication interceptor at all (`src/main/java/com/appsecco/dvja/controllers/ApiAction.java:39-44` and `src/main/resources/struts.xml:156-159`); (3) three confirmed SQL/JPQL injections and one OS command injection, each traced end-to-end from request parameter to sink (`UserService.java:75`, `ProductService.java:48`, `PingAction.java:45`). Coverage included the Struts entry points, the Java controllers and services, the data model, the JSP views cited by a finding, the Struts/Spring/Log4j2/Docker configuration, and `pom.xml`; it did not cover actual runtime behavior, git history, vendored third-party front-end libraries (jQuery, Font Awesome), full transitive-dependency resolution, or any dynamic testing (see "What was not covered"). Method: entry points first, data traced from source to sink, one finding per sink, exact line quoted, confidence stated, then every finding mechanically verified against the locked tree by `verify-safety-report.mjs`.
